## Aim and data

Some meta-analyses include trials that report only **one** subgroup
(for example invasive ventilation only, with no non-invasive row). This
vignette asks how **contribution-adjusted meta-analysis (CAMS)** and
the older **DA / AD / SWADA** constructions behave on such a **mixed**
table: trials with two subgroups alongside trials with one.

We use two package examples for contrast:

- **`respire_age`** (RESPIRE ciprofloxacin DPI trials): both age strata
  (**`<65`**, **`>=65`**) in every study— a **complete** table (see
  **`vignette("comparing-da-ad-swada")`**).
- **`steroids`**: WHO REACT corticosteroids in COVID-19 (mortality ORs
  by ventilation support). Seven trials; **IV** (invasive) and **NIV**
  (non-invasive) rows when both exist. **CoDEX**, **DEXA-COVID 19**, and
  **RECOVERY** contribute **IV only** (no within-trial IV–NIV pair).

IV-only trials can inform an **IV** treatment effect. They do not
contain a within-trial IV-versus-NIV contrast, so they cannot identify
the interaction \(g_j=y_{\mathrm{IV},j}-y_{\mathrm{NIV},j}\) from that
trial alone.

Below we fit **DA**, **AD**, **SWADA**, and **frequentist CAMS**
(`method = "REML"`) on **`steroids`**. Those first three are
**different constructions**, not alternative CAMS models
(`vignette("comparing-da-ad-swada")`). The CAMS map is
`vignette("cams")`.

```{r load}
library(interactmeta)
library(metafor)
```

**`library(metafor)`** is for **`escalc()`** on the 2×2 mortality counts
( **`interactmeta`** also exports **`escalc()`** after **`library(interactmeta)`** ).

```{r steroids-pattern}
st <- steroids[steroids$n > 0, ]
table(st$study, st$subgroup)
```

## Single-subgroup trials in CAMS (not “missing data”)

CAMS is defined on **paired** subgroup rows per trial (rotation into
\(m_j\) and \(g_j\)). A trial that reports **only IV** is a **single-subgroup
data constellation**, not “missing information” in the survey sense: there
was never an NIV estimate to omit.

**Model limit.** If the unreported subgroup had infinite sampling variance
(precision zero), its precision share would be zero and \(\pi_j\) would
be 1; the interaction contrast \(g_j\) would carry no within-trial
information from that study. That is the conceptual limit CAMS targets.

**Implementation.** To keep a rectangular long table for **`ifrac()`** /
**`cams()`**, **`ifrac()`** completes the absent cell with a **placeholder**
(`yi = 0`, `vi = big_var`, default **`big_var = 100^2`** on **`cams()`**).
That is a **numerical device** so the design matrix and **`metafor`**
fitters can run; it is **not** a Bayesian “continuity correction” and
not a claim that NIV was observed with log OR zero. With large
**`big_var`**, \(\pi_j\approx 1\), \(\mathrm{Var}(g_j)\) is huge, and
the trial is **essentially silent** in the interaction fit while still
contributing to the overall \(m_j\) meta-regression—matching the limit
above. You can change **`big_var`** via **`cams(..., big_var = ...)`**;
see **`?ifrac`**.

**DA / AD / SWADA** require two cells on every trial for a like-for-like
table here, so **`ifrac()`** completes the design once; all four fits use
the same completed **`des`**. Mortality odds ratios come from **`escalc()`**
on the event counts.

```{r steroids-fit, cache = TRUE}
steroids_es <- escalc(
  measure = "OR",
  ai = treat.events,
  bi = treat.total - treat.events,
  ci = cont.events,
  di = cont.total - cont.events,
  data = st
)
des <- ifrac(steroids_es, reference = "Non-IMV")
fit_da_st <- da(des, reference = "Non-IMV")
fit_ad_st <- ad(des, reference = "Non-IMV")
fit_sw_st <- swada(des, reference = "Non-IMV")
fit_cams_st <- cams(des, reference = "Non-IMV", method = "REML")
```

```{r steroids-des-print}
head(des)
```

## Where the interaction comes from

The interaction is identified by the complete trials. Under default
interaction random-effects (RE) weights, AD, SWADA, and CAMS
\(\gamma\) agree. DA does not: it still uses the IV-only trials in the
IV series.

```{r steroids-int}
compare(
  fit_da_st,
  fit_ad_st,
  fit_sw_st,
  fit_cams_st,
  exponentiate = TRUE
)
```

```{r steroids-weights}
compare_weights(fit_da_st, fit_ad_st, fit_sw_st)
```

RECOVERY and CoDEX take a large share of the DA **IV** weights and
essentially none of the AD/SWADA weights. That is the SWADA principle
on a mixed table: shared interaction weights silence trials that do
not identify \(g_j\).

## The two pooled information fractions

Trial \(\pi_j\) is design and does not change. What can change is the
reporting mix \(\omega=\sum_j\pi_j w_j/\sum_j w_j\).

The package default `ifrac = "interaction"` is the interaction
information fraction. The weights are the interaction-block
inverse-variance weights

$$
w_j=\frac{1}{\tau_\gamma^2+\mathrm{Var}(g_j)},
\qquad
\mathrm{Var}(g_j)=\sigma_{Aj}^2+\sigma_{Bj}^2.
$$

`ifrac = "overall"` is the overall information fraction (IF)
[@panaro2025cams, eq. 3.16]. The weights are the
overall-block inverse-variance weights

$$
w_j=\frac{1}{\tau^2+v_j},
\qquad
v_j=\mathrm{Var}(m_j)=(1-\pi_j)^2\sigma_{Aj}^2+\pi_j^2\sigma_{Bj}^2.
$$

```{r steroids-ifrac-overall}
ifrac(fit_cams_st, ifrac = "overall")
```

```{r steroids-ifrac-interaction}
ifrac(fit_cams_st, ifrac = "interaction")
```

The two \(\omega\) differ because the IV-only trials dominate one
weighting and are silent in the other. They sit at \(\pi_j\approx 1\)
with \(\mathrm{Var}(m_j)\approx\sigma_{\mathrm{IV},j}^2\), so RECOVERY
in particular pulls overall \(\omega\) toward 1. The same trials have
very large \(\mathrm{Var}(g_j)\) from the placeholder cell, so
interaction \(\omega\) is a reweighting of the **complete** trials only.

Switching `ifrac` does not change a trial's \(\pi_j\) and does not
refit \(\gamma\). It changes which trials dominate the reporting mix
used by `modifiers()`, `combined()`, and `forestplot()`.

```{r steroids-forest-overall, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 6}
forestplot(
  fit_cams_st,
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  ifrac = "overall"
)
```

Overall and Prediction at the overall mix.

```{r steroids-forest-interaction, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 6}
forestplot(
  fit_cams_st,
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  ifrac = "interaction"
)
```

Overall and Prediction at the interaction mix.

```{r steroids-sg-overall}
modifiers(fit_cams_st, exponentiate = TRUE, ifrac = "overall")
```

```{r steroids-sg-interaction}
modifiers(fit_cams_st, exponentiate = TRUE, ifrac = "interaction")
```

If \(\omega\) is meant to represent the trials that identify the
treatment-by-subgroup interaction, `ifrac = "interaction"` matches
that block. At that mix the CAMS subgroup odds ratios sit next to
SWADA. DA's IV odds ratio does not: that series is still using the
IV-only trials. The `il6` table is the same incomplete-table pattern
on concomitant corticosteroids.

## Summary

Single-subgroup trials are a **design pattern**, not missing cells in
the imputation sense. They can inform a subgroup-specific treatment
effect without informing the within-trial interaction. AD, SWADA, and
CAMS base \(\gamma\) on trials that identify \(g_j\); DA can still use
single-subgroup trials in a subgroup-specific series.

In CAMS, `ifrac = "overall"` versus `ifrac = "interaction"` changes
the pooled information fraction \(\omega\) used for
contribution-dependent summaries. It does not change the fitted
interaction. On a mixed table the two mixes differ because
single-subgroup trials can dominate \(\mathrm{Var}(m_j)\) weights and
are silent in \(\mathrm{Var}(g_j)\) weights.
